properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: Current Situation – May 19; 2026 Overnight; due to the low relatively humidity; steady winds across the island; and the alignment of canyons with those winds; the fire remained active. Growth was predominately to the north on the eastern half of the fire. Grasses on the island continue to be receptive to fire with the dry winds; low humidity; and warm days. On the eastern side of the fire footprint; the fire is approximately ½ mile south of the Water Canyon Campground and just south of the Main (Soledad) Road. The fire has moved through the Torrey Pines area on the east side of the island and continues to have a northward progression. Today; firefighters will continue to focus on defensible space preparation of the structures in the Main Ranch Complex. They will also be focusing on structures within the Water Canyon area recognizing the fire has potential to reach Cherry Canyon. On the west side of the fire; one of the fire crews will work to make their way to the South Point Lighthouse area to establish containment through direct suppression actions. More firefighters and equipment such as additional UTV’s; fire hose and pumps will be arriving on the island along with resupplies for the firefighters already on the island. This includes a hotshot crew; a wildland fire module; and an unmanned aircraft module; the latter to aid in visual reconnaissance of the fire’s activity and location across the steep and rugged terrain – including a visual inspection of the Torrey Pines. The incident management team is also working on getting specialized wildland fire engines onto the island by midweek to engage in the firefighting effort. This morning; aircraft will once again be over the island to assess the potential for water and limited retardant drops by air tankers; the latter when needed for imminent protection of assets and values at risk. Slightly weaker winds are forecast but still strong on the ridges. Background: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Closures: The National Park Service has closed Santa Rosa Island to day use and overnight use at least through this week due to the wildfire. Visitors with campground reservations at Water Canyon Campground have been notified via e-mail. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed.
